summary.text: Methanogens are anaerobic archaea that produce methane as a byproduct of their energy metabolism.
Making methane is their only way to generate ATP, and its enzymes are so sensitive to oxygen that they are exclusively anaerobic.
They live in wetlands, rice paddy soil, landfills, wastewater plants and animal digestive tracts, where they remove excess hydrogen and fermentation products.

facts.label: Deep ice find
facts.value: Live methane-makers found about three kilometres under Greenland

items.prompt: Why are methanogens mostly found in oxygen-free places rather than in open air?

options.label: Open air holds too much carbon dioxide for them
The enzymes in their methane pathway are extremely sensitive to oxygen
They can feed only on animal tissue
Their cells cannot survive above freezing

items.explain: Methanogens are exclusively anaerobic because of the extreme oxygen sensitivity of methanogenesis enzymes.

items.prompt: In an oxygen-free swamp, other microbes leave behind hydrogen and fermentation products. What do methanogens do with them?

options.label: Consume them, which clears the excess
Turn them into oxygen for the other microbes
Ignore them and feed on dead plants
Store them as fat for later

items.explain: In anaerobic environments methanogens remove excess hydrogen and fermentation products made by other microbes.

items.prompt: A student claims every methanogen is an extremophile. What is the better statement?

options.label: None are, because they all live in ordinary conditions
All are, because oxygen-free places count as extreme
Some are, but most live in ordinary conditions at near-neutral pH
Only those in animal guts are

items.explain: Some methanogens are extremophiles, but most isolates are mesophilic and grow around neutral pH, and most of their environments are not extreme.

items.prompt: A rover detects methane in the air of Mars. Why does that raise the possibility of life?

options.label: Only living animals are able to make methane
Methane is commonly generated by underground microbes such as methanogens
Methane is the gas that plants breathe in
Methanogens were already found in Martian rock samples

items.explain: Methane is commonly generated by underground microbes such as methanogens, so its detection signals a possibility of life.

items.prompt: A friend notes that some plants and animal cells also make methane, so they must be methanogens. Is that right?

options.label: Yes, any methane-making cell counts as a methanogen
Yes, as long as the cell lives without oxygen
No, because the methane they make is a different gas
No, in them the pathway differs and does not feed their energy supply

items.explain: All known methanogens belong to Archaea, and methane production in other organisms differs and does not contribute to ATP formation.

items.prompt: Most methanogens, unlike bacteria, lack a peptidoglycan wall. What do most have instead?

options.label: A protein array that fits together like a jigsaw puzzle
A thick shell of cellulose
A wall of chitin like that of fungi
A hard shell of silica

items.explain: Methanogens lack peptidoglycan, and most have a paracrystalline protein array, the S-layer, that fits together like a jigsaw puzzle.
